documents.title: Audit programme · staff payroll
documents.letterhead:
Bapat Venkatesh & Co., Chartered Accountants
Audit programme
documents.subject: Staff payroll · interim audit 2026–27
body: ## 1. Headcount
- Roll the April headcount forward: add joiners from their start month; take leavers out from the month after their last working day. Compare with the heads paid and explain every difference.
## 2. Joiners
- An appointment letter signed by an authorised person, with the pay the register shows.
- Attendance from the first month, a UAN, and salary paid into an account in the employee’s own name that no one else is paid into.
- The master entry approved by someone other than the person who made it.
## 3. Leavers
- Last working day from the accepted resignation. Salary up to that day and not after; F&F paid; the exit entered in the master before the next salary run.
## 4. PF and ESI (December 2026)
- PF, employee’s share: 12% of PF wages, with PF wages capped at ₹25,000 from 17 September 2026 (₹15,000 before), or the actual PF wages if lower.
- ESI, employee’s share: 0.75% of ESI wages, rounded up to the next rupee, where ESI wages are ₹21,000 a month or less.
## 5. Bank
- December net pay in the register agrees with the bank’s salary credit report, name by name, and no account is paid twice.
## 6. Controls
- Note who enters changes to the master and who approves them, and whether anyone checks the salary register before the bank file goes.

tasks.title: Roll the headcount forward
tasks.prompt: Roll the April headcount forward to two payrolls: September, the half-year, and December, our interim date. Take joiners and leavers from the dates in the employee master, then compare with the heads the payroll actually paid. Your sheet goes to Aditi when you move on.

lockOnLeave.ask: Hand your headcount sheet to Aditi?
lockOnLeave.note: You can’t change it after this.
lockOnLeave.done: Handed to Aditi. You can read your sheet but not change it.

hints: A leaver is paid for the month they leave and drops out the month after.
A joiner counts from the month they start, even if that is the 7th.

cells.line: Add: joiners who started in or before that month

sep.working: Pooja 1 July, Rakesh 1 August, Neha 7 September

dec.working: Pooja, Rakesh, Neha; Sameera starts on 4 January 2027

cells.line: Less: leavers who left before that month

dec.working: Vinod, Amit, Hemant; Meera leaves on 31 December

notes.join.sep: Rakesh counts: the master gives him a joining date. Whether he exists is a question for the joiner tests.
notes.leave.sep: Vinod left in June and Amit on 31 August. Hemant and Meera were still here in September.
notes.diff.sep: September paid 45 heads against 44 expected: one salary too many. Amit left on 31 August and should have dropped out of the September run.
notes.join.dec: Sameera went into the master on 28 December but starts on 4 January 2027. The start date counts, not the entry. Still three.
notes.leave.dec: Meera’s last day is 31 December, so she drops out in January. Still three.
notes.diff.dec: December ties, 43 and 43, which is where Varun stopped. A tie only says the payroll agrees with the master, and the master holds Rakesh.

items.note: Rakesh: no letter on file, no biometric, no UAN, no ID card. Sunil entered him on 1 August, approval blank. His ₹27,800 goes into account 04170166931667, which the bank shows as Sunil’s. ₹1,40,000 gross to December. Exception, and nothing shows a January salary is due.

tasks.title: Recompute December PF and ESI
tasks.prompt: Recompute the employee’s share of PF and ESI on the rows Aditi marked yellow in the December register, taking PF wages and ESI wages as the sheet shows them. Rates and ceilings are in the audit programme. Enter what each should be, 0 where nothing is due. Your figures go to Aditi when you move on.

lockOnLeave.ask: Hand your PF and ESI figures to Aditi?
lockOnLeave.note: You can’t change them after this.
lockOnLeave.done: Handed to Aditi. You can read your figures but not change them.

hints: From 17 September 2026 PF wages stop at ₹25,000, not ₹15,000. Below the cap, take the actual PF wages.
ESI is due only where ESI wages are ₹21,000 or less.

notes.pf1002.due: Venkat’s PF wages are ₹1,09,200, far above the cap. From 17 September 2026 the cap is ₹25,000, so ₹3,000 against the ₹1,800 deducted.
notes.pf1005.due: Datta’s PF wages are ₹30,150. On the ₹25,000 cap that is ₹3,000; the sheet’s formula still says MIN(…, 15000), so it deducted ₹1,800.
notes.pf1018.due: Pallavi’s PF wages, ₹23,900, are under the new cap, so the actual wages count: ₹2,868. The sheet took ₹15,000 and deducted ₹1,800.
notes.pf1031.due: Anil’s ₹16,650 is under ₹25,000: 12% is ₹1,998. Only the old cap made it ₹1,800.
notes.pf1068.due: Shrikant’s ₹15,350 is just over the old cap, so the sheet cut him to ₹1,800. On actual wages it is ₹1,842.
notes.pf1036.due: Santosh’s ₹14,300 is under both caps, so the change does nothing for him: ₹1,716, as deducted.
notes.esi1052.due: ESI is deducted in whole rupees, and any paise round up: ₹148.50 becomes ₹149, as the sheet has it. Ganpat’s and Nikhil’s round the same way.
notes.esi1018.due: Pallavi’s PF goes by her PF wages, ₹23,900; her ESI goes by her ESI wages, ₹46,000, far above ₹21,000. Nil is right.

tasks.title: Write your points for Aditi
tasks.prompt: Aditi wants one note with today’s points. It stays inside the firm until Rehan and Sudha have read it. Pick the right line for each point; the change register, bank report, F&F papers and salary register are in Documents.
hints: Write what each paper shows, names included. What it means, and what happens to anyone, is for Rehan and Sudha.
For the control point, read the change register’s two name columns and the foot of the salary register.

options.text: E1093 Rakesh Bhoir: a fake employee that Sunil Gaikwad created on 1 August 2026 to draw a second salary into his own account, 04170166931667. Sunil has taken ₹1,40,000 gross so far and should be suspended from all payroll work before the January salary run.
options.why: The facts behind it may all be true, but “fake” and “taken” are conclusions, and “suspended” a decision, for Rehan and Sudha after they look. Our note says what the papers show.

options.text: E1093 Rakesh Bhoir: entered on 1 August 2026 with the approval blank; no appointment letter on file, and no biometric record, ID card or UAN. His salary goes into account 04170166931667, held at the bank by Sunil Gaikwad. ₹1,40,000 gross paid to December.
options.why: Facts only, each from a paper: the change register, the missing file, the attendance, the ID cards and the bank report. Sunil’s account is what makes it serious.

options.text: E1093 Rakesh Bhoir: entered on 1 August 2026; his joining papers are with Production, his biometric enrolment is pending and his UAN is still to come, so HR will complete the file. ₹1,40,000 gross paid to December.
options.why: That is HR’s story, not evidence: five months with no letter on file, no punch and no UAN, while his pay lands in Sunil’s account.

options.text: Next: I have mailed Sunil to explain the shared account and to send Rakesh Bhoir’s joining papers by Wednesday, so that we can close this point and pay E1093 as usual in January.
options.why: That warns the one person whose account the money goes into, gives papers two days to appear and pays E1093 again in January. Nothing about E1093 goes to Sunil.

options.text: Next: I have asked Shabana to delete E1093 from the master today and to recover the ₹1,40,000 from Sunil’s January salary, so that the January salary run goes out clean and nothing more is lost to him.
options.why: Deleting the entry destroys the record we need, and a recovery from Sunil assumes a finding nobody has made yet. Neither is ours to ask for.

options.text: Next: I have not raised E1093 with Shabana or Sunil. Please take it to Rehan and Sudha before the January run, so they decide what happens to the payment, with the records kept as they are.
options.why: It goes up the line before anyone at Tamhini hears of it, and nothing is touched. How it is taken up is for Rehan and Sudha.

options.text: E1044 Amit Wagh: last working day 31 August 2026, F&F paid on 15 September, yet the September run paid him a full month, ₹31,000 gross and ₹29,000 net to his account. His exit reached the master only on 5 October. To recover.
options.why: The acceptance letter and the F&F fix the last day; the register shows September paid anyway. The late master entry is the cause, and the point for Shabana.

options.text: E1044 Amit Wagh: last working day 31 August 2026, F&F paid on 15 September, and the September run paid him ₹31,000 gross as his leave encashment, settled with the F&F. His exit was entered in the master on 5 October. Nothing to recover.
options.why: His leave encashment was 12 days, ₹6,440, paid with the F&F. The ₹31,000 is a full month’s salary for September, after he had left.

options.text: E1044 Amit Wagh: last working day 31 August 2026, F&F paid on 15 September, and the September run paid him ₹31,000 gross as notice pay agreed in his F&F. His exit reached the master on 5 October. Nothing to recover.
options.why: His F&F says notice was served in full and pays no notice pay. The September money is salary for a month he did not work.

options.text: PF: the ceiling is ₹25,000 from 17 September 2026, but only for employees who joined after that date. Existing staff stay on the ₹15,000 cap, so the sheet is right and all eight December rows I recomputed agree with it. No arrears are due.
options.why: It covers existing staff too: PF wages capped at ₹15,000 now go up to ₹25,000, or the actual PF wages if lower. The audit programme sets one cap for everyone.

options.text: PF: the ceiling is ₹25,000 from 17 September 2026, but the sheet still caps PF wages at ₹15,000. Five of eight rows I recomputed are short, E1005’s by ₹1,200, and Tamhini’s matching share with them. Arrears since the change to be worked out.
options.why: Below the new cap the actual PF wages count, so Santosh, Neha and Baban were already right. The rest stay short until Shabana fixes the formula.

options.text: PF: the ceiling is ₹25,000 from 17 September 2026, so every employee’s PF is now ₹3,000 a month, 12% of ₹25,000, whatever the wages. All eight December rows I recomputed are short. Arrears since the change to be worked out.
options.why: ₹25,000 is a cap, not a fixed wage. Where PF wages are lower, 12% of the actual wages applies: Santosh’s ₹1,716 was right.

options.text: Control: the payroll controls work, since Shabana approves master changes and the December register agrees with the bank report. E1093 and Amit are one-off slips at Sunil’s desk, so a reminder to him to enter changes on time is enough for now.
options.why: E1093 went in with no approval at all, and the register agreeing with the bank only proves the bank paid what the sheet said. Nobody checks the sheet itself.

options.text: Control: Sunil should come off payroll work today and the salary run should move to the accounts team from January, with Mahesh signing every payment. I will tell Shabana so at this evening’s closing meeting, so that it is in place before the January run.
options.why: That settles Sunil’s case before Rehan and Sudha have looked, and tells HR today. The note names the gap and the check that closes it; who runs payroll is Tamhini’s call.

options.text: Control: Sunil makes every master change and prepares the salary register, and nobody checks the register before the bank file goes. E1093 went in unapproved; Amit’s exit went in after the September run. A joiner and leaver check before each run would catch both.
options.why: The change register and the foot of the salary register show it: one person makes the changes and the run, and E1093 went through with the approval blank. The check is a recommendation; what it means for Sunil is for Rehan and Sudha.

freeText.label: Your own line for the note

passNeeds.note: The seven calls do not count the same: Rakesh counts four times, Amit twice. Get more right to pass.

wrap.text: One of the seven has nothing behind him but a master entry and a salary, and Amit was paid for a month after he left. December’s headcount still tied. I’ve called Rehan; he and Sudha will read your note before anyone at Tamhini hears of it. The PF formula goes to Shabana once they agree.

wrapPartial.text: Before this note goes anywhere, check each call against the papers, not against Shabana’s file note or Varun’s chat. I’ll take the note to Rehan myself this afternoon.

wrapRetry.text: The bank report shows the extra salary once you put each name next to the account it is paid into. Then match each leaver’s last working day to the months they were paid, and recompute PF with the ₹25,000 cap: below it, the actual PF wages count.

model.intro: Two of the seven are exceptions. Rakesh Bhoir has a master entry and a salary, nothing else, and the salary goes into an account the bank holds in Sunil Gaikwad’s name. Amit Wagh was paid for September after leaving on 31 August. The headcount tied in December all the same. The sheet still caps PF wages at ₹15,000, and nobody checks the sheet before the bank file goes.

principles: A headcount that ties can still hide a ghost: test every joiner against a letter, attendance, a UAN and a bank account of their own.
Take a suspected ghost to your senior as facts from the papers, before anyone at the client hears of it, and leave every record as it is.
Recompute PF on the ceiling for the days the wages cover: ₹25,000 from 17 September 2026, ₹15,000 before, or the actual PF wages if lower.

interview.q: How would you find a ghost employee on a payroll?
interview.checking: Whether you know the tests behind the word, or only the word.
outline: I roll the headcount forward, then test every joiner: letter, attendance, UAN and an account of their own.
A PF or tax deduction proves only that the sheet worked it out, not that the person exists.
In the simulation December’s headcount tied, yet one joiner’s salary went into the payroll assistant’s account.

interview.q: How did you recompute PF, and what changed in 2026?
interview.checking: Whether you know the rate and the ceiling, and that the ceiling moved in 2026.
outline: The employee pays 12% of PF wages up to the ceiling, and the employer matches it.
The ceiling rose from ₹15,000 to ₹25,000 on 17 September 2026; below it, actual wages apply.
In the simulation the sheet used the old ₹15,000 cap[[; five of eight rows I recomputed were short{pfShort|}]].
